# Summary
<!-- Summary of the change. -->
This PR introduces a modified navigation system and holding the last version of photo and description in **FitScreen** going back from **PreviewScreen**.  

# What
<!-- Briefly list what changed, grouped by area below. Remove any subsection that doesn't apply. -->

- MainActivity 
  - Added `.popBackStack()` function in **PreviewItemScreen** composable to get the preserved state in **FitCheckScreen**

# Why
<!-- Motivation, links to issues, and any design decisions or trade-offs. -->
This bug is discovered during one of the UX tests. One of our users mentioned that the selected photo and written description is not preserved when they were moving to the next screen and going back again. This bug is fixed by replacing `onGoBack = { navController.popBackStack() }` inside **PreviewItemScreen** composable lambda because previously, returning from PreviewItemScreen, it recreates the FitCheck destination, i.e. , new VM instance. Thus, the original **FitCheckViewModel** is discarded, so its image resets to URi.EMPTY. Hence, I used `.popBackStack()` to popping the screen from stach which preserves the saved state.  

# Screenshots / Videos

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eed7f679-db1c-49c5-a229-e98c7f66d37c

author: scala-steward
edoakes
body:
Follow up to this comment: https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/57641#discussion_r2546349957

With the code change above, we require the "bidi reactor" to have a shared pointer to itself, which keeps the object alive until `OnDone` is called by gRPC, while also allowing us to take a `weak_ptr` to avoid use-after-free in async callbacks.

I've cleaned this up a bit to enforce that all reactors are shared_ptrs using a static factory method. This uses the same strategy that we have in a few other places ([example](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/blob/c9e020bcb0eb6007640fc161959c59badccea9e3/src/ray/object_manager/plasma/connection.h#L57)) to use a private struct to prevent callers from calling the constructor while still making it public so that `make_shared` can be used.

Originally I tried removing the self pointer entirely and only using `shared_from_this`, but the way the code is structured right now with callbacks up and down between `ray_syncer.cc` and the reactors, I was not confident that it would be safe.

body:
## PR Type
What kind of change does this PR introduce?

<!-- Please check the one that applies to this PR using "x". -->

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Other... Please describe:


## What is the current behavior?
<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->

Issue Number: #2844

SSH includes config files alphabetically via `Include ~/.ssh/qinglong/*.config`. Global keys named `global_global.config` match before subscription configs like `my-repo.config` or `xyz-subscription.config`. SSH uses first matching Host, causing global keys to override subscription-specific keys.


## What is the new behavior?

Global SSH config files now use `~global_${alias}` prefix instead of `global_${alias}`, ensuring they load last alphabetically. The tilde character (`~`) is ASCII 126, the highest printable ASCII character, guaranteeing the global config always loads last regardless of subscription naming. Subscription-specific keys match first; global keys act as a guaranteed fallback.

**Changes:**
- `addGlobalSSHKey`: Updated to use `~global_${alias}` naming
- `removeGlobalSSHKey`: Updated to match new naming scheme

**Why tilde (~) prefix:**
- Tilde is ASCII 126, the highest printable ASCII character (only DEL at 127 is higher but unusable in filenames)
- SSH's Include directive uses glob expansion which sorts by byte order
- Ensures global config loads last even if subscriptions use 'zzz' or any other alphanumeric prefix
- Extensively tested with edge cases including `zzzzzzz.config` and other boundary conditions
- Valid filename character on Unix/Linux systems


## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

<!-- If this PR contains a breaking change, please describe the impact and migration path for existing applications below. -->


## Other information

Existing global keys will continue to work but won't be automatically migrated. Users should remove and re-add global SSH keys after upgrade to apply the new naming scheme.

- Fixes whyour/qinglong#2844

body:
# 🚀 Fix: Inconsistent Loading States in Team Member Cards

## Description

This PR fixes a UX issue where team member cards displayed loading states inconsistently when expanding to view daily plans and tasks. The authenticated user's card showed proper skeleton loading indicators, while other team members' cards loaded data with a visible delay without any loading feedback.

[ETP-168 [Bug]-[Web] Inconsistent Loading States in Team Member Cards](https://evertech.atlassian.net/browse/ETP-168?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiOTljMDIxMTY3ZjJmNDNmOThjYmNhMzExYzA5ZTY3YTEiLCJwIjoiamlyYS1zbGFjay1pbnQifQ)

**What problem does this PR address?**
- Team member cards lacked consistent loading states across all users
- Non-authenticated users' cards showed no visual feedback during data fetching
- Permission logic was overly restrictive, preventing proper loading state display

**What changes were made?**
- Added proper loading state consumption from `useDailyPlan` hook
- Fixed permission logic to use `canSeeActivity` helper instead of exact user ID matching
- Implemented conditional rendering with skeleton loaders for all team members
- Improved data synchronization logic to prevent data loss during refetching

**Why are these changes useful?**
- Provides consistent UX across all team member cards
- Improves perceived performance with proper loading feedback
- Prevents user confusion during data loading phases
- Ensures data integrity during React Query refetching cycles

## What Was Changed

### Major Changes

**1. Team Member Card Loading States**
- Added `useDailyPlan` hook import to access loading states
- Imported `UserProfileTaskSkeleton` component for consistent loading UI
- Created `isLoadingMemberData` computed value from `profileDailyPlansLoading`
- Replaced restrictive permission check (`member.employee?.userId === user?.id`) with `canSeeActivity` helper
- Implemented conditional rendering: skeleton during loading, content when loaded
- Applied fix across all three view modes (Card, Table, Block)

**2. Team Data Synchronization** (`apps/web/core/hooks/organizations/teams/use-teams-state.ts`)
- Improved `setTeamsUpdate` function with intelligent merge strategy
- Added protection against data loss during React Query refetching
- Implemented conditional member preservation logic:
  - If new data has `members` array (even empty), use it (complete data)
  - If new data has `undefined/null` members, preserve existing members (incomplete data)
- Prevents race conditions during polling/refetching cycles

**3. React Query Configuration** (`apps/web/core/hooks/organizations/teams/use-organization-teams.ts`)
- Optimized query configuration for better performance:
  - Increased `staleTime` to 10 minutes (from default)
  - Increased `gcTime` to 30 minutes (from default)
  - Disabled `refetchOnWindowFocus` to reduce unnecessary refetching
  - Disabled `refetchOnReconnect` to reduce unnecessary refetching
- Improved data loading logic in `loadTeamsData` function
- Enhanced error handling and logging

### Minor Changes

- Added JSDoc comments for better code documentation
- Improved code readability with clear variable naming
- Removed unused code and imports
- Consistent code formatting across modified files

## How to Test This PR

1. **Setup**:
   ```bash
   yarn start:web:dev
   ```

2. **Navigate to Team Members Page**:
   - Open browser at `http://localhost:3030`
   - Log in with your credentials
   - Navigate to the team members page (`/`)

3. **Test Loading States**:
   - Click the `ChevronToggleButton` to expand different team member cards
   - Verify that ALL team members show skeleton loaders during data fetch
   - Confirm that loading states appear consistently across:
     - Current user's card
     - Other team members' cards
     - All three view modes (Card, Table, Block)

4. **Test Permission Logic**:
   - Verify that `canSeeActivity` permission is respected
   - Confirm that users without permission don't see expanded content
   - Check that loading states still appear for permitted users

5. **Test Data Integrity**:
   - Expand multiple team member cards
   - Wait for data to load
   - Verify that all team members remain visible (no disappearing members)
   - Refresh the page and confirm data persists correctly

6. **Performance Check**:
   - Monitor network tab for reduced refetching
   - Verify that data is cached properly (10-minute stale time)
   - Confirm no unnecessary API calls on window focus/reconnect

## Screenshots (if needed)

### Before
- ❌ Other team members' cards: No loading indicator, blank state during fetch
- ❌ Inconsistent UX between current user and other members
- ❌ Data occasionally disappeared after loading

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/889bd6d9-b074-4aef-aa38-17036182c215

### After
- ✅ All team members' cards: Consistent skeleton loading indicators
- ✅ Uniform UX across all team members
- ✅ Data remains stable during refetching cycles

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6f064a5-772f-42b5-8f17-7f6d5743c777

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (fixes a problem)
- [ ] New feature (adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (requires changes elsewhere)
- [ ] Documentation update

## ✅ Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project coding style
- [x] I reviewed my own code and added comments where needed
- [x] I tested my changes locally
- [x] I updated or created related documentation if needed
- [x] No new warnings or errors are introduced

## Notes for the Reviewer (Optional)

**Key Implementation Details**:
- The loading state fix is straightforward: consume existing `profileDailyPlansLoading` from `useDailyPlan` hook
- Permission logic change from exact user ID match to `canSeeActivity` is more flexible and correct
- Data merge strategy in `setTeamsUpdate` prevents race conditions during React Query refetching
- React Query configuration changes reduce unnecessary network requests while maintaining data freshness

**Testing Focus Areas**:
- Verify loading states appear for ALL team members (not just current user)
- Confirm data doesn't disappear after initial load
- Check that performance improvements don't break existing functionality
- Test across different permission levels and team sizes

**Known Considerations**:
- React Query cache configuration (10-minute stale time) balances performance and data freshness
- Member preservation logic assumes API may return incomplete data during refetching
- Loading states use existing `UserProfileTaskSkeleton` component for consistency

This PR adds support for `SIZE` annotations to the ASN.1 API, starting with fields of type `SEQUENCE OF`.

```python
@asn1.sequence
class Example
  a: Annotated[typing.List[int], asn1.Size(min=1, max=5)]  # SIZE(1..5)

@asn1.sequence
class Example
  a: Annotated[typing.List[int], asn1.Size(min=1, max=None)]  # SIZE(1..MAX)


@asn1.sequence
class Example
  a: Annotated[typing.List[int], asn1.Size.exact(6)]  # SIZE(6)
```

```ruby

# update_coveralls_repo(repo["name"], @github_installation_id)
```

**What's Needed:**

The tool currently adds repositories to the GitHub App installation on GitHub's side, but it **does NOT update the Coveralls database** to reflect this change.

**Required Actions:**

1. **Create or identify Coveralls API endpoint** for updating a repository's `github_install_id`:
   - Endpoint format: `PATCH https://coveralls.io/api/repos/github/{org}/{repo}` (suggested)
   - Required fields to update:
     - `github_install_id` → Set to the GitHub App installation ID
     - Possibly: `github_app_disabled` → Set to `false`

2. **Implement `update_coveralls_repo` method** in `cli.rb`:
   ```ruby
   def update_coveralls_repo(repo_name, installation_id)
     owner, repo = parse_repo_name(repo_name)
     url = "#{COVERALLS_API_BASE}/repos/github/#{owner}/#{repo}"

     response = HTTP.headers(
       accept: JSON_HEADER,
       "Authorization" => "token #{@coveralls_token}"
     ).patch(url, json: {
       github_install_id: installation_id
     })

     unless response.code == 200
       raise Thor::Error.new "Error updating Coveralls repo: #{response.code}"
     end
   end
   ```

3. **Uncomment the TODO line** in the migrate method (line 146)

4. **Add test coverage** for database update functionality

**Database Fields Reference:**

```ruby

- name: "coverallsapp"                     # Org name
- user_id: 149163
- state: "active"
- org: true
```

**Alternative Approaches:**

If a PATCH endpoint doesn't exist:
1. **Backend Script**: Create a separate Rails console script to bulk update the database

3. **Trigger-based**: Coveralls could detect the GitHub App installation via webhook and auto-update

author: vv21buhtig
body:
…afe SaveChangesAsync

- **App.xaml.cs**: Modified `EnsureAdminUserExists` to rely on `DatabaseService.SaveChangesAsync` instead of direct `SaveChangesAsync` calls; removed redundant `await dbService.SaveChangesAsync()` call.
- **Data/AppDbContext.cs**: Removed inline connection string configuration; moved all settings to DI registration for consistency and maintainability.
- **Data/Repository/GameRepository.cs**: Removed `await _context.SaveChangesAsync()` inside `CreateGameAsync`; now defers save to `DatabaseService`.
- **Data/Repository/MoveRepository.cs**: Removed `await _context.SaveChangesAsync()` inside `CreateMoveAsync`; deferred save to `DatabaseService`.
- **Data/Repository/UserRepository.cs**: Removed `await _context.SaveChangesAsync()` inside `CreateUserAsync`; now defers save to `DatabaseService`.
- **Services/DatabaseService.cs**: Added `SemaphoreSlim` to prevent concurrent access to `_context.SaveChangesAsync`; centralized and synchronized all database write operations through `SaveChangesAsync`.

**Summary:** The error was caused by multiple async operations attempting to start new transactions while previous ones were still active in the same session. By removing `SaveChangesAsync` calls from repository methods and centralizing them in `DatabaseService` with thread-safe synchronization via `SemaphoreSlim`, the issue is fully resolved. All database writes are now properly serialized, preventing transaction conflicts.

author: mjq
body:
Currently, transaction name clustering and normalization happens [partly in Relay](https://github.com/getsentry/relay/blob/aad4b6099d12422e88dd5df49abae11247efdd99/relay-event-normalization/src/transactions/processor.rs#L23) and partly in [Sentry's `event_manager.save_transaction_events`](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/blob/e3a640e44a05512236eefc64a5934443666f8a5a/src/sentry/event_manager.py#L2663). This normalization only applies to transactions, and spans that are extracted from those transactions.

For standalone spans and OTLP spans, we need to apply the clustering elsewhere. We will introduce it into the segment enrichment step of the span ingestion pipeline.

This PR introduces the first step of the process, stripping identifier-like patterns out of names that aren't explicitly parameterized (via the `sentry.span.source` attribute). Future PRs will add interactions with the transaction clusterer (saving seen names and applying compiled clustering rules).

The changes are behind an org flag (`organizations:normalize_segment_names_in_span_enrichment`) for testing and easy rollback.

Closes ENG-5953.

author: anutosh491
body: # Description Hi, Today while building xeus-cpp on emscripten-forge's emscripten-4x branch, I saw this This was expected because 1) with emsdk 3.1.73 we are using the Emscripten EH model (which is pulls in the invoke_*** functions/symbols) 2) with emsdk 4-x, emscripten promotes using the wasm EH model. Hence emscripten-forge's emscripten-4x branch builds all hosted packages (xeus, llvm and everything involved using `-fwasm-exceptions` and `-sSUPPORT_LONGJMP=wasm`) 3) We need to replicate the same using clang's webassembly toolchain (https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/main/clang/lib/Driver/ToolChains/WebAssembly.cpp#L357-L452) - using `-fwasm-exceptions` pulls in the following ``` -target-feature +exception-handling -target-feature +multivalue -target-feature +reference-types -exception-model=wasm -mllvm -wasm-enable-eh ``` - and `-sSUPPORT_LONGJMP=wasm` which is an emcc specific flag boils down to `-mllvm -wasm-enable-sjlj` which can be used through clang. So basically we end up replicating the same result but with a different exception handling model. ## Type of change Please tick all options which are relevant. - [ ] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Added/removed dependencies - [ ] Required documentation updates

author: copilot
body:
Replaces the dummy `/api/predict` endpoint with `/api/predict/sql` that executes SQL queries against PostgreSQL and runs ML inference using pre-trained models.

## Changes

- **New endpoint**: `POST /api/predict/sql` with `predict_by_sql()` handler
  - Executes user-provided SQL queries via `psycopg2`
  - Supports flexible model selection: direct path, filename, prefix-based auto-detection
  - Applies feature engineering pipeline: label encoding → scaling → prediction
  - Returns structured responses: `{"ok": true, "result": [...]}` or `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}`

- **Core logic**: `sql_predict(payload)` function
  - Validates required columns match model's feature schema
  - Handles unknown categories in encoded fields (assigns -1)
  - Properly manages DB connections with cleanup

- **Dependencies**: Added `pandas` and `scikit-learn` to requirements.txt

- **Documentation**: Created `backend/API_DOCUMENTATION.md` with request/response formats and error codes

## Example Usage

```python
# Request with auto-detection (finds latest model matching prefix)
{
  "sql": "SELECT term, subj, crse, sec, credits FROM courses WHERE term = 202501",
  "model_prefix": "enrollment_tree_min_",
  "features": "min"
}

# Response
{
  "ok": true,
  "result": [
    {"index": 0, "prediction": 12.48, "term": 202501, "subj": "BUS", "crse": "101", ...},
    ...
  ]
}
```

In diesem PR wird künftig eine festgeschriebene dbversion in die Objekt, als auch Historientabellen eingebettet, in welchem die zum Zeitpunkt genutztes DB-Schema protokolliert wird. Dies ist im Hintergrund relevant, um nachzuvollziehen, mit welchen bestehenden Regeln der konkrete Eintrag erstellt worden ist. 

Dies ist in Fällen relevant, wo sich die Bedeutung der jeweiligen Aktion mit der Zeit verändern und gegebenenfalls in einer neueren Version anders gehandhabt werden können.

Um den Code Testen zu können, müssen auf Datenbankebene folgende Änderungen vorgenommen werden:
`ALTER TABLE ams_Historie_Objekt ADD dbversion LONGTEXT NOT NULL;`  
`ALTER TABLE ams_Objekt ADD dbversion LONGTEXT NOT NULL;`
`update ams_Objekt set dbversion="0.9";`  
`update ams_Historie_Objekt set dbversion="0.9";`
In der konkreten Migration müsste der Defaultwert auf "1.0" gesetzt werden.


Diese PR wird für anderweitige PRs benötigt, die konkrete Änderungen am Datenbankschema durchführen, sodass nicht alle potentiell relevanten Funktionen enthalten sind:

-  Sicht der Versionsangabe in den Details des jeweiligen Objekts
-  Eine Informationsseite mit dokumentierten Änderungen des Datenbankschema bzw. deren Auswirkungen

This is part of the _https://jira.intuit.com/browse/MSGR-446_ ticket to transfer the code from golang internal version of the infobib API to the official version in java.  This subsection will transfer the requestAPI portion.
**Implementation summary**
We first needed to recreate the structure of the requestAPI in java.  For instance the notion of context is integrated in golang but not in java so we add to create new classes to handle that.  Also, the architecture is very different.  The internal version is very extensively articulated with many sub trees whereas the infobib java version works with mainly 2 sub trees (model and api). Finally in order to achieve build success we needed to modify the pom.xml file
**Risk mitigation**
We created junit that ran successfully to cover the requestAPI operations.

author: tlisanti
body:
Built on top of changes in https://github.com/confidentsecurity/compute-sepolicy/pull/22.

Adds additional permissions for `vllm_t` so that the vLLM server can log usage stats to /var/log/vllm.log and expose a /metrics endpoint to gather metrics.

_Copied description from @mwalkiewicz 's PR_:
Should be used with something like this https://github.com/confidentsecurity/T/commit/be6626a9f56f1be29d24934da24dea70a6f6cfd8.
Running `restorecon -R /tmp/hf_home /tmp/vllm_cache /models/vllm` should be run before vllm starts up.
Instead of granting access to all initrc_tmp files I think we should rather label our dirs in /tmp and /models as vllm_data_t . 
Appropriate file context patterns for these directories are already in .fc in the policy, but these files do not exist when then relabeling is performed in compute-base builder so we have to set it manually. 

In the aforementioned commit I've proposed running this command before starting up vllm and it works, but maybe it's not the best way to do it. Other options include relabeling in initramfs but I did not want to add anything there myself unless necessary or setting a default label for /ollama mount, this second options looks nice but we'd still need to relabel files in /tmp or move them to /ollama.

author: kingst
body:
This commit adds logic to support backfilled CGM values from CGM managers. There are a few key corner cases that it handles:
    - _Not_ backfilling previously deleted CGM readings
    - Deduplication for CGM readings
    - Avoiding adding CGM readings when values already exist
    
The way we handle it is by comparing timestamps from both the DeletedGlucoseStored and GlucoseStored CoreData tables.
    
Our logic isn't perfect, because we're only looking at timestamps. But it's simple and predictable. Since these are corner cases that we don't expect to happen often in practice, having a less than perfect but simple solution is preferred.

This PR depends on this one, which adds the deleted glucose archive: https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/pull/851

author: copilot
body:
Builds a tool to analyze Steam libraries, fetch game completion times from HowLongToBeat, aggregate review scores, and rank games by playtime/quality to help decide what to play next.

## Architecture

**API Integrations** (3 modules)
- `steam_api.py` - Fetches owned games via Steam Web API
- `hltb_api.py` - Queries HowLongToBeat for main story completion times
- `review_api.py` - Retrieves Steam user review scores (percentage-based)

**Core Logic** (`main.py`)
- Enriches Steam library with HLTB + review data
- Filters games without HLTB data
- Sorts by playtime (asc), then score (desc)
- Outputs human-readable text + JSON

**Infrastructure**
- `cache.py` - File-based cache with 24h TTL to minimize API calls
- Rate limiting (0.5s HLTB, 0.3s reviews)
- Graceful error handling; individual failures don't halt processing

## Usage

```bash
# Demo mode (no credentials required)
python3 demo.py

# Production mode
cp .env.example .env  # Add STEAM_API_KEY and STEAM_ID
python3 main.py
```

**Output example:**
```
1. Portal
   Playtime: 3.5 hours (main story)
   Score: 95.2% (Steam) - Overwhelmingly Positive
   Steam: https://store.steampowered.com/app/400/
   HLTB: https://howlongtobeat.com/game/7231
```

## Configuration

Requires Steam Web API key and Steam ID. Template provided in `.env.example`.

Large libraries (100+ games) take 10-30+ minutes on first run due to rate limiting. Subsequent runs use cache.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Build a script that:
> 
> Fetches my entire Steam library using the Steam Web API (owned games with app IDs, names, etc.).
> 
> Queries HowLongToBeat for each game and retrieves:
> 
> Main Story time
> 
> Fetches a game review score (Metacritic, Steam user score, or OpenCritic — whichever is easiest).
> 
> Filters out any games that have no HowLongToBeat data.
> 
> Sorts the remaining games by:
> 
> shortest playtime first,
> 
> highest score within the same time range.
> 
> Outputs a clean, human-readable list or JSON with:
> 
> game name
> 
> playtime (main story)
> 
> review score
> 
> link to Steam page
> 
> link to HLTB page
> 
> The code should be modular, clean, documented, and use best practices.
> 
> Use Python with requests (or Node.js with fetch, depending on what I write next).
> 
> Add error handling and caching to avoid unnecessary repeated calls.
> 
> Goal:
> Create a tool that helps me decide “what should I play next?”, ranking short, high-quality games from my Steam backlog.


</details>

author: radik878
body:
## Changes

Replaced all uses of Signature.BytesWithRecovery in XDC RLP encoders with direct streaming via StartByteArray, Write of R/S spans and WriteByte for recovery id. This preserves exact RLP output while removing a byte[65] allocation from each encode call on hot serialization paths such as quorum and timeout certificates. RlpStream already exposes span-based APIs, so no API changes to Signature are required and we retain its Vector512-based storage. Other areas where a byte[] is truly required (e.g., header fields and tests) are left intact to maintain existing data model contracts. This change reduces GC pressure and improves throughput

#### What types of changes does your code introduce?

- [x] Optimization

**Backend Setup and Database Integration**
* Added PostgreSQL integration with secure connection settings, and a helper to create the `users` table if it does not exist in `db.js` and `users.js` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f5a42ac2e8b2cd33d61dcec43f2551dbbb3827581ecb438038d4cdcc6800e577R13) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a67e374b6a18d6267cd58fb680ad0cf28caea62c5b131d42354ea5ee9222e28fR2-R20).

* Ensured the users table is created before starting the server, and changed the static file serving logic to serve the frontend directory.

**Frontend User Experience Enhancements**
* Added password visibility toggle styling and logic for both signup and login forms (`signup.css`, `login.css`, `login.js`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d04b51c8ce33fe3a2b1c01abb5cda98f6d1658d29f8ca38e239520285ce22f09R44-R66) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c2013333fa6171c4ff89a0e42e11cb5ca879df824acb64010b441418beff9979R41-R67) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7f05a9fe9b3199c5cd475e5ce11710d93049da60a55155d886686686a84c0c93R1-R46).
* Implemented custom popup messaging for login feedback in `login.js` and corresponding styles in `login.css` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d04b51c8ce33fe3a2b1c01abb5cda98f6d1658d29f8ca38e239520285ce22f09R95-R124) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7f05a9fe9b3199c5cd475e5ce11710d93049da60a55155d886686686a84c0c93R1-R46).

**Documentation**

author: fw-bot
body:
There is an issue with conditionally visible snippets in `mass_mailing` where a user is able to undo in the editor the reset of a filter caused by a recipient model change.

How to reproduce:
- Create a mass_mailing and add a conditional display rule on a snippet
- Change the recipient model
- undo, then redo

Issue:
- The rule appears again on the element, even though the model still has the new value. The domain is invalid, since it applied only on the previous model

Resolution:
- Make the `data-filter-domain` a `system_attribute` so it is not registered in the editor history. To inform the view that there was a change, `onChange` is called directly when the attribute value changes.

body:
Fixes all security vulnerabilities identified in the Middle Number Game application by reverting to the original secure implementation.

## Security Fixes

### Code Injection
- Removed `eval()` vulnerability in `submitNumber()`
- Restored `parseInt()` with proper numeric validation
- Added validation to reject non-numeric input

### XSS Vulnerabilities
- Removed `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` usage for player names and submissions
- Restored safe React text rendering for all user-controlled data
- Removed raw user input display that enabled XSS attacks

### Prototype Pollution
- Removed vulnerable `merge()` function that didn't guard against prototype pollution
- Removed `cloneObject()` function that propagated the vulnerability
- Eliminated all unsafe object cloning operations

### Authentication Bypass
- Removed `resetAllRooms()` admin backdoor function
- Eliminated weak client-side authentication checks
- Removed unauthorized access to privileged operations

### Information Disclosure
- Removed database path exposure in UI (`numrooms/{roomID}/unamesnum`)
- Removed user session details from page rendering
- Eliminated debug information from production code

### Insecure Data Storage
- Removed localStorage usage for user data (`lastUser`, `lastRoom`)
- Removed sessionStorage usage for game state
- Eliminated persistent storage of sensitive information

### Input Validation
- Restored `type="number"` on number input fields
- Restored `pattern="[a-z]{3,}"` validation on text inputs
- Re-enabled browser-level validation for room names and usernames

### Error Message Exposure
- Removed detailed error alerts showing internal error details
- Kept secure console.error logging for debugging

## Validation

- ✅ All MiddleNumber tests passing (9/9)
- ✅ CodeQL security scan: 0 alerts
- ✅ All identified vulnerabilities addressed
- ✅ Original secure functionality restored

author: vikram-kangotra
body:
The issue occurred because ReadDir was being consumed by the for loop, causing it to be dropped immediately after iteration. This closed the directory file descriptor (FD 3) before metadata() could be called on the entries, since /proc/self/fd shows the process's own open FDs.

By using read_dir.by_ref() in the loop, we borrow the iterator instead of consuming it, keeping the ReadDir (and its underlying FD) alive until enter_directory() completes.

Fixes: #9332

This pull request migrates the gesture recognition backend from MediaPipe's TFLite-based classifier to a new PyTorch-based classifier, updates configuration and documentation accordingly, and revises the gesture label set and associated mappings. The changes ensure that the system now uses a PyTorch model for gesture recognition, with new gestures and updated device command mappings.

**Backend Migration to PyTorch:**

- Added a new `PytorchGestureRecognitionInterface` implementation in `src/core/interfaces/gesture_recognition_interface/PytorchGestureRecognitionInterface.py`, which uses MediaPipe for hand landmark extraction and a PyTorch model for gesture classification.
- Added a new PyTorch keypoint classifier model and loader in `src/gesture_recognition/keypoint_classifier_pytorch.py`.
- Updated configuration files (`config/full/default.json`, `config/full/deploy.json`, `config/full/single_machine_default.json`) to use `PytorchGestureRecognitionInterface` instead of `MediaPipeGestureRecognitionInterface`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f136e26a18881e3ce61ea348a6b8fbc87dd73adf5ea938249195fcb0162f1c16L40-R40) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-50180112ce8e56312eab93b8792c43226443be53d3f588cc0acc34e2c9457737L37-R37)

**Model and Documentation Updates:**

- Modified the model download script (`scripts/download_models.py`) to fetch the new PyTorch model checkpoint.
- Updated documentation to reflect PyTorch support and installation requirements in `README.md` and `docs/models.md`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L31-R31) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R45-R48) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4a20043f76a669ac926c5fe98226490f44635620f8f20e27f2703b7eb46a4b2eL27-R28)

### Key Technical Details Documented

**Attendance Calculation Logic:**
```python
# Overlap detection algorithm
session_overlaps = (
    login_time <= class_end and 
    logout_time >= class_start
)
# Creates attendance records for all overlapping classes
```

**ESP32 RFID Flow:**
```
Card Scan → UID Read → Serial TX (115200 baud) → 
Python Script → DB Lookup → Login/Logout Toggle → 
Attendance Calculation (if logout)
```

**Database Cascade Behavior:**
```sql
DELETE students → CASCADE delete login_logout → SET NULL attendance.login_logout_id
DELETE classes → CASCADE delete attendance records
```

body:
## Summary

Refactor `compute_delta()` and `compute_gamma()` to reuse the PDE `CenteredDifference` operators instead of manually implementing finite difference formulas. This eliminates ~60 lines of duplicated code while maintaining identical numerical accuracy and zero performance regression.

## Changes

### Code Quality Improvements
- **60 lines removed**: Eliminated manual finite difference formulas
- **Single source of truth**: Greeks and PDE solver share operator implementation
- **Automatic grid handling**: Uniform and non-uniform (sinh-spaced) grids work transparently
- **SIMD-ready**: Automatic vectorization available for future batch operations

### Implementation Details

1. **Task 1**: Extract `find_grid_index()` helper - deduplicate grid search logic (949b067)
2. **Task 2**: Add `CenteredDifference` member to `AmericanOptionSolver` (f4f8bff)
3. **Task 3**: Add lazy initialization helper `get_diff_operator()` (ce4f410)
4. **Task 4**: Refactor `compute_delta()` to use operators (845996c)
5. **Task 5**: Refactor `compute_gamma()` to use operators (a3ccff4)
6. **Task 6**: Performance verification (d965c28)
7. **Task 7**: Documentation updates (99dd79a)
8. **Task 8**: Fix example move semantics (6e75010)

### Performance Verification

**Greeks Computation:**
- Before: 1276 ns
- After: 1277 ns
- Change: +0.08% (within measurement noise)

**Full Benchmark Suite:**
- American option pricing: No change (~2.6 ms)
- Batch processing: No change (~7.3 ms)
- IV calculation: No change (~24 ms)

**Verdict:** Zero performance regression

### Testing

- ✅ All 38 tests passing
- ✅ All examples building
- ✅ Numerical accuracy maintained (same finite difference formulas)
- ✅ Performance verified (zero regression)

## Benefits

**Code Reuse (DRY Principle):**
- Greeks and PDE solver share operator implementation
- Maintenance updates benefit both automatically

**Maintainability:**
- Simpler code (no manual grid spacing calculations)
- Clear separation of concerns (operators vs business logic)
- Easier to extend with higher-order Greeks

**Correctness:**
- Uses battle-tested operators from PDE solver
- Handles non-uniform grids automatically via GridSpacing
- Identical numerical accuracy verified by tests

**Performance:**
- Zero overhead from lazy initialization
- SIMD acceleration available (3-6× on large grids)
- Virtual dispatch cost negligible (<5ns) vs computation (~1300ns)

## Documentation

- Added Greeks calculation section to CLAUDE.md
- Created completion summary: `docs/plans/2025-11-20-greeks-refactoring-completion.md`
- Performance verification report: `PERFORMANCE_VERIFICATION_GREEKS_REFACTORING.md`

- Implementation plan: `docs/plans/2025-11-20-greeks-use-pde-operators.md`

author: ealanisln
body:
#### Summary

- Implemented a robust SSE endpoint for admin realtime driver tracking with strong TypeScript typing and safer stream lifecycle management.
- Refined the driver-facing live map and added an end‑to‑end Playwright spec that exercises the admin dashboard together with the new Test Driver Simulator.
- Ensured the feature flag–driven realtime flow remains safe to roll out, with clean fallbacks and no TODOs/`any` left in the new path.

#### Features/Changes

- **Admin SSE endpoint (`GET /api/tracking/live`)**
  - Added explicit TypeScript row interfaces for the three raw Prisma queries (active drivers, recent locations, active deliveries) and wired them into `prisma.$queryRawUnsafe<...>()` for type safety.
  - Normalized `active_deliveries` to a numeric count in a defensive way (accepts number or string from the DB, treats NaN as 0).
  - Kept the improved SSE controller safety: checking `controller.desiredSize` before enqueue, cleaning up intervals on close/cancel, and logging to Sentry on failures.

- **Driver live map**
  - Updated `DriverLiveMap` to:
    - Use `MAP_CONFIG.MAX_AUTO_ZOOM` (instead of an undefined `DRIVER_VIEW_ZOOM`) when first centering on the driver, avoiding a runtime/TS mismatch.
    - Preserve existing behavior: initial center and zoom, trail rendering via `driver-trail` GeoJSON source, and optional delivery markers.

- **Realtime E2E coverage**
  - Added `e2e/realtime-driver-tracking.spec.ts` to validate the end‑to‑end flow:
    - Navigates to `/admin/tracking` and skips gracefully if authentication is required.
    - Detects whether the realtime UI (WebSocket/SSE toggle, connection text) is present and skips if feature flags are disabled.
    - Opens `/admin/tracking/test-driver` in a second tab, connects the Test Driver Simulator, and starts the route simulation.
    - Asserts that the admin dashboard shows “Real-time WebSocket connected” and renders key realtime driver metrics (`On Duty`, `GPS Updates`) without errors.

#### Testing

- **Manual / local**
  - Verified driver map and test driver simulator behavior in development with realtime flags enabled.
  - Confirmed SSE endpoint streams structured JSON updates for drivers, locations, and deliveries without throwing.

- **Automated**
  - **TypeScript**: `pnpm typecheck`  
    - ✅ Passes after tightening the raw query typing and config usage.
  - **Lint**: `pnpm lint` and the lint step during `pnpm build`  
    - ✅ Complete with existing warnings only (React hooks dependencies and one `import/no-anonymous-default-export` in the `mapbox-gl` mock), none in the three modified files.
  - **Jest**: `pnpm test`  
    - ❌ Fails due to **existing issues** in orders/driver‑assignment tests (e.g. `toast.error is not a function`, `filteredDrivers.slice is not a function`, and multiple long‑running tests timing out).  
    - These are pre‑existing and unrelated to the realtime tracking changes; no code in `SingleOrder`, `DriverAssignmentDialog`, or their tests was modified here.
  - **Playwright**: `pnpm test:e2e -- e2e/realtime-driver-tracking.spec.ts`  
    - ❌ Fails early if `TEST_CLIENT_EMAIL` and other required test env vars are not configured locally; once `.env.test`/CI secrets are complete, this spec should run as intended.
  - **Build**: `NODE_OPTIONS='--max-old-space-size=4096' pnpm build`  
    - ✅ Succeeds; Next.js emits existing Supabase Edge-runtime warnings and ESLint suggestions, but no new errors from this branch.

#### Database Changes

- **Migrations**: None.
- **Schema**: SSE queries read from existing tables (`drivers`, `driver_shifts`, `driver_locations`, `deliveries`) only.
- **Rollback strategy**:
  - Since this is a code‑only change, rollback is simply reverting this PR.
  - If a rollback is required after deployment, you can disable the realtime features via feature flags (see Deployment Notes) to fall back to existing SSE/REST behavior.

#### Breaking Changes

- **API surface**:
  - `GET /api/tracking/live` response shape and semantics remain compatible; the change is strictly typing and robustness inside the handler.
- **Client behavior**:
  - `DriverLiveMap` still uses Mapbox with the same markers and trail; only the zoom constant was corrected to an existing config key.
- No breaking changes are expected for existing admin or driver flows.

#### Deployment Notes

- **Environment variables**
  - Ensure the following are set in your runtime environment for realtime tracking:
    - `NEXT_PUBLIC_FF_USE_REALTIME_TRACKING`
    - `NEXT_PUBLIC_FF_USE_REALTIME_LOCATION_UPDATES`
    - `NEXT_PUBLIC_FF_USE_REALTIME_ADMIN_DASHBOARD`
    - `NEXT_PUBLIC_FF_REALTIME_FALLBACK_TO_SSE`
    - `NEXT_PUBLIC_FF_REALTIME_FALLBACK_TO_REST`
    - `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN` (required for `DriverLiveMap` and admin tracking maps).
  - For e2e in CI/local:
    - `TEST_CLIENT_EMAIL` (plus any other variables referenced in `e2e/auth/setup.ts`) must be present in `.env.test` or CI secrets.

- **Post‑deployment checks**
  - Open `/admin/tracking` and confirm:
    - Realtime/SSE toggle is visible when flags are enabled.
    - “Real-time WebSocket connected” text appears when in WebSocket mode.
  - Navigate to `/admin/tracking/test-driver` and:
    - Connect the simulator and start the route.
    - Observe driver count and GPS updates on the admin dashboard.

- **Rollback**
  - To disable the new realtime paths without reverting code:
    - Set the three core realtime feature flags to `false` and redeploy; the system will fall back to the existing non‑realtime modes.

#### Reviewer Checklist

- [ ] Code follows TypeScript/Next.js best practices (typed Prisma raw queries, no `any` in new paths, App Router conventions).  
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, and `pnpm build` pass locally.  
- [ ] Jest failures are understood as pre‑existing in the orders/driver‑assignment test suite; no new test regressions introduced by this PR.  
- [ ] Documentation and env requirements for realtime and Mapbox are clear (`README.md`, `docs/testing/REALTIME_TESTING_CHECKLIST.md`).  
- [ ] No unnecessary console logs, TODOs, or unrelated file changes are present in the diff.

This PR updates the **Linux NuGet build pipeline** to support the switch from **ARM64 Linux** to **AzureLinux** VMs.

author: divyanshu-s13
body:
<!-- What issue does this PR close? -->
Closes #197 


## 📝 Description

This PR fixes a critical bug where the BasicDetails form component was accepting invalid user input without any validation or error feedback. Users could submit empty required fields, malformed emails, invalid phone numbers, and incorrect URLs without any warnings or prevention. This compromise data integrity and causes backend errors.

The fix implements comprehensive client-side validation with real-time error feedback, helping users enter correct information before submission.

## 🔧 Changes Made

### Form State Management
- Added controlled form inputs connected to React state for both Influencer and Brand forms
- Implemented separate form data objects for influencer and brand user types
- Added error state management to track validation errors

### Validation Functions
- ✅ `validateEmail()` - Validates email format using regex pattern
- ✅ `validatePhone()` - Validates international phone number format
- ✅ `validateURL()` - Validates HTTP/HTTPS URLs using URL constructor
- ✅ `validateStep()` - Step-specific validation based on user type and current step

### Input Validation Rules Implemented

**Influencer Form - Step 0 (Basic Details):**
- First Name: Required, non-empty string
- Last Name: Required, non-empty string
- Email: Required, valid email format (contains @ and domain)
- Phone: Required, valid international phone format
- Category: Required selection

**Influencer Form - Step 1 (Social Media):**
- Instagram Handle: Optional, must start with @
- YouTube Channel: Optional, valid URL
- Website: Optional, valid URL

**Influencer Form - Step 2 (Audience):**
- Audience Size: Required, positive number
- Engagement Rate: Required, 0-100%
- Main Platform: Required selection
- Audience Age: Required selection

**Brand Form - Step 0 (Company Info):**
- Company Name: Required, non-empty string
- Website: Required, valid URL
- Industry: Required selection
- Company Size: Required selection
- Budget: Required selection

**Brand Form - Step 1 (Campaign Preferences):**
- Target Audience: Required selection
- Preferred Platforms: Required selection
- Campaign Goals: Required selection

### User Experience Improvements
- Real-time validation feedback with error messages displayed below invalid fields
- Visual error indicators: Red borders on invalid inputs
- Error icons with AlertCircle from lucide-react
- Required fields marked with red asterisk (*)
- Errors automatically clear when user fixes the field
- Next button disabled until all current step validations pass
- Form data persists across step navigation

### Code Quality

I've successfully implemented validation to ensure that Credit payment method retail sales can only be returned using the Credit payment method. Changes Made: 1. Backend Validation (SaleReturnController.java): New Methods Added: - validateCreditReturnPaymentMethod() (line 572-593): Validates that Credit sales can only be returned using Credit payment method - getOriginalPaymentBill() (line 601-631): Helper method that navigates bill references to find the payment bill - isOriginalBillCredit() (line 1261-1267): Public getter for UI to check if original bill was Credit Modified Methods: - settle() (line 633-675): Added call to validateCreditReturnPaymentMethod() at line 605-607 2. UI Enhancement (pharmacy_bill_return_retail.xhtml): Line 226-232: Added a warning alert that displays when the original bill used Credit:
Credit Return: This sale was paid using Credit. The return must also use Credit payment method only.
Line 237: Disabled the payment method dropdown when original bill is Credit: disabled="#{saleReturnController.originalBillCredit}" How It Works: 1. When a Credit sale is selected for return: - The system automatically pre-selects Credit as the return payment method - A warning message displays informing the user that only Credit can be used - The payment method dropdown is disabled (grayed out) to prevent changes 2. If someone tries to bypass the UI restriction: - The backend validation in settle() method will catch it - Error message: "This sale was paid using Credit payment method. Returns must also use Credit payment method only." - The return transaction will be blocked 3. For non-Credit sales: - Everything works as before - Users can select any payment method for the return Testing: You can now test this by: 1. Creating a retail sale with Credit payment method 2. If you try to return using another payment method (by modifying the request), the backend will block it ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added validation requiring returns of credit-paid sales to also use Credit payment. * Added warning notification alerting users when Credit payment is mandatory for returns. * Restricted payment method selection when returning sales originally paid with Credit to ensure payment consistency. ✏️ Tip: You can customize this high-level summary in your review settings.

author: kacper808128
body:
Bug: Word-based scoring used substring matching which caused incorrect matches. Example: "Poland" matched "Antigua and Barbuda" because "poland".includes("and") returned true.

Fix: Changed from substring matching to exact word matching:
- Before: optWords.some(ow => ow.includes(aw) || aw.includes(ow))
- After: optWords.includes(aw)

Now words must match exactly, not just contain each other as substrings.

Fixes: content.js:380

author: justiceleeg
body:
## Problem
The `UpdateChatMessageIntent` function was not persisting the `is_intent_render` flag to the database, even though:
- The `Intent` type includes `IsRender` 
- The database schema has `is_intent_render` column
- The intent detection logic correctly identifies render requests

This caused render jobs to be triggered (via `EnqueueRenderWorkspace`) but the database flag remained `false`, making it impossible for the frontend to detect render intent via database queries.

## Solution
Added `is_intent_render = $7` to the UPDATE query and `intent.IsRender` to the Exec parameters.

## Testing
- [x] Verified render intent is now saved to database
- [x] Verified existing render job triggering still works
- [x] Checked that database queries for `is_intent_render` now return correct values

body:
Contact form appeared to work but logs weren't created and emails weren't received. Root cause: critical logging and mail operations were conditional on `BBX_DEBUG_RECAPTCHA` flag, causing silent failures in production.

## Changes

**contact-submit.php** (37 lines):

- **Logging now unconditional**: Removed all `if (BBX_DEBUG_RECAPTCHA)` gates from critical log paths
- **Enhanced error capture**: Added `error_get_last()` to surface mkdir/file_put_contents failures with actual error messages
- **Fallback mechanism**: Log to error_log if file operations fail instead of silently dropping data
- **Mail visibility**: Always log mail recipient configuration and mail() dispatch status

### Before
```php
if (defined('BBX_DEBUG_RECAPTCHA') && BBX_DEBUG_RECAPTCHA) {
    error_log('CONTACT FORM DEBUG: entering bbx_log_contact_submission()...');
}
// ... mkdir fails, function exits, no trace
```

### After
```php
// Always log function entry for debugging
error_log('CONTACT FORM DEBUG: entering bbx_log_contact_submission() with status=' . $status);

if (!mkdir($logDirectory, 0755, true)) {
    $mkdirError = error_get_last();
    error_log('CONTACT FORM LOG ERROR: mkdir() error: ' . $mkdirError['message']);
    // Continue to fallback logging instead of exiting
}

// Always write fallback to error_log if file write fails
error_log('CONTACT FORM LOG FALLBACK: ' . $jsonLine);
```

## Impact

- Every submission now leaves complete trace in error_log (entry → directory → file → mail)
- No data loss on failure (fallback to error_log)
- Mail delivery status always visible
- Directory/file permission issues immediately diagnosable

## Documentation

- `QUICK-START-CONTACT-FORM-FIX.md` - Deployment test procedure
- `CONTACT-FORM-FIX-ANALYSIS.md` - Root cause analysis
- `SECURITY-SUMMARY.md` - No vulnerabilities introduced

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

PROMPT TIL ALPHA-Web-Diagnostics-Agent

Alpha til ALPHA-Web-Diagnostics-Agent – dette er en **priority one** mission.

### 🎯 Mission

Løs kontaktformular-pakken én gang for alle:

1. **Kontaktformularen** på `https://blackbox.codes/contact.php` skal:

   * Validere input og reCAPTCHA korrekt.
   * Skrive en JSON-linje pr. submission til `logs/contact-submissions.log`.
   * Sende mail til **[ops@blackbox.codes](mailto:ops@blackbox.codes)** med alle relevante detaljer.
   * Lægge tydelig status i `error_log` (debug + fejl).

2. **CI/CD** for dette skal være stabil:

   * Deploy fra `main` skal altid lægge **den nyeste** `contact-submit.php` ud.
   * Smoke-tests må ikke “grønnemarke” noget, der reelt er brudt (fx hvis logging eller mail fejler).

### 🧩 Kendte fakta

Repo: `AlphaAcces/ALPHA-Interface-GUI`
Relevante filer:

* `contact.php` – selve formen (HTML/JS).
* `assets/js/site.js` – AJAX + reCAPTCHA token.
* `contact-submit.php` – backend (validering, reCAPTCHA, logging, mail()).
* `includes/env.php` – bbx_env + BBX_RECAPTCHA_* + RECAPTCHA_DEBUG.
* `.github/workflows/ci.yml` – CI & Deploy (Secure).
* Log-struktur på serveren (cPanel/Apache):

  * PHP error log: `/home/blackowu/public_html/error_log`
  * Formularlog (forventet): `/home/blackowu/public_html/logs/contact-submissions.log`

Miljø:

* RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY / SECRET_KEY / PROJECT_ID + RECAPTCHA_DEBUG sættes via `.htaccess`.
* CI/CD bruger FTP/FTPS til at deploye `main` til `public_html`.

### 🔎 Symptomer (nu)

* Frontend viser “Tak for din henvendelse!”, så brugeroplevelsen ser ok ud.
* `error_log` viser **BBX ENV DEBUG** for RECAPTCHA-nøgler (alle [SET]), så env/load virker.
* **Men**:

  * `logs/contact-submissions.log` findes stadig ikke på serveren.
  * Der er (endnu) ingen mail i Proton på `ops@blackbox.codes`.
  * Vi ser ikke de forventede `CONTACT FORM …` loglinjer i `error_log` (fx mail debug, log_write debug).

Med andre ord: koden ser rigtig ud i repoet, CI kører grønt, men **drifts-adfærden er ikke på plads**.

### 🔧 Din opgave – trin for trin

1. **Analysér koden i repoet**

   * Gå igennem:

     * `contact.php`
     * `assets/js/site.js`
     * `includes/env.php`
     * `contact-submit.php`
   * Bekræft at flowet er:

     1. Inputvalidering (name/email/message)
     2. reCAPTCHA (Enterprise + Standard fallback)
     3. Logging via `bbx_log_contact_submission(...)`
     4. Mailafsendelse til `ops@blackbox.codes`
     5. JSON-respons til frontend
   * Notér præcis hvilke steder der kaldes:

     * `file_put_contents` på `logs/contact-submissions.log`
     * `mail()`.

2. **Sikre at logging ALDRIG kan “forstumme”**

   * Sørg for at `bbx_log_contact_submission()`:

     * Altid forsøger at oprette mappen `__DIR__/logs` (med mkdir + clear error_log ved fejl).
     * Altid skriver en fallback-JSON til `error_log`, hvis `file_put_contents` fejler.
     * Altid logger tydeligt til `error_log`, når logning lykkes (`CONTACT FORM DEBUG: Successfully logged…`).
   * Lav en lille intern “self-test” helper (kan være midlertidig), som gør det nemt at se i `error_log`, at log-funktionen rent faktisk er blevet kørt.

3. **Sikre at mail-delen er 100% entydig**

   * Tjek at kontakt-modtageren ender som:

     * `ops@blackbox.codes` (evtl. via `CONTACT_EMAIL` env, men med fallback til denne).
   * Omkring `mail()` skal der logges:

     * `CONTACT FORM MAIL DEBUG: about to send mail to …`
     * `CONTACT FORM MAIL DEBUG: mail() dispatched to …` **eller**
     * `CONTACT FORM WARNING: mail() failed for …`
   * Ved mail-fejl:

     * Brugeren må godt stadig se success-besked (for ikke at afsløre mail-infrastruktur),
       men det skal være **krystalklart** i `error_log`, at mail-delen fejlede.

4. **CI/CD-integritet**

   * Bekræft, at `.github/workflows/ci.yml` rent faktisk deployer seneste `contact-submit.php`.
   * Hvis du finder et mismatch (fx caching på FTP, index.html resten, osv.), så:

     * Dokumentér det kort.
     * Tilbyd en minimal patch til workflowet, som sikrer at:

       * De relevante filer overskrives hver gang.
       * Smoke-testing fanger fejl (fx at `contact-submit.php` ikke svarer som forventet).

5. **Lever en konkret patch**

   * Alle nødvendige ændringer i:

     * `contact-submit.php`
     * evt. `includes/env.php`
     * evt. CI/workflow-filer
   * Du skal lave minimal men fuldt dækkende patch:

     * Logging → altid synlig i `error_log` ved succes/fejl.
     * `contact-submissions.log` → altid oprettet/appendet, eller forklaret via fallback‐log.
     * Mail → entydigt til `ops@blackbox.codes` og logget.

6. **Afslut med en kort, brugbar rapport**

   * Diff-oversigt: liste over filer + 1 linjes beskrivelse per fil (hvad og hvorfor).
   * Manuel testplan (til mennesket “Alpha”), fx:

     1. Udfyld og send kontaktformular på `https://blackbox.codes/contact.php`.
     2. Forvent grøn success-besked i UI.
     3. I cPanel: tjek at `logs/contact-submissions.log` har en ny JSON-linje.
     4. Tjek i `error_log` at du ser...

</details>


> **Custom agent used: ALPHA-Web-Diagnostics-Agent**
> Elite-agent til dybdegående fejlsøgning og stabilisering af webstacken for ALPHA-Interface-GUI – inkl. kontaktformular, reCAPTCHA, mail-delivery, logging, CI/CD-deploy og cPanel-miljø.

This pull request introduces a centralized error handling system to the backend, improving how errors are managed and reported throughout the Express application. It adds custom error classes for common scenarios, a global error handler middleware, and an async handler utility to streamline error propagation from route handlers. Additionally, it updates the main application setup to use these new error handling mechanisms for both API and non-API routes.

**Error handling improvements:**

* Added custom error classes (`AppError`, `AuthenticationError`, `AuthorizationError`, `NotFoundError`, `ValidationError`) to represent different operational errors and HTTP status codes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0a6301564cbdd7ea713d0cb67ce1446fc093b3f40b17799cedf07cc308f62fcdR1-R25) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-776d7af679bd27649ffd9feea0614c3fb8c3b372344d1227d8b2d862610149a7R1-R12) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5121441128c81e50a1ef920a84ede497b620f80d4ab12608ef93d2e128ad139dR1-R13) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-967259e87af43aec33f6ca2245b6cbea0ee7e40e2df6118d007379838f38d6edR1-R13) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-d0ff7ddae0af4277b62552a87a444bb05f7ed2c72b1b3eb523420431a648583cR1-R12)
* Centralized all error exports in `middleware/errors/index.ts` for easier imports and management.
* Implemented a global error handler middleware (`errorHandler`) that maps known errors (including validation and JWT errors) to standardized HTTP responses, with stack traces in non-production environments.

**Express app setup changes:**

* Registered the global error handler after all routes and middleware in `index.ts`, ensuring all errors are processed consistently.
* Added middleware to handle non-existing API and root routes by forwarding 404 errors to the error handler using `NotFoundError`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c20200a666b149a045e365999f581db8e04687cfc9569bdf4c9477cab954d324R5-R6) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c20200a666b149a045e365999f581db8e04687cfc9569bdf4c9477cab954d324R17-R36)

**Async error propagation:**

* Introduced `asyncHandler` utility to wrap async route handlers, automatically forwarding rejected promises and thrown errors to the error pipeline, reducing boilerplate and ensuring consistent error handling.

Closes #15

<!-- If you're making a doc PR or something tiny where the below is irrelevant, delete this
template and use a short description, but in your description aim to include both what the
change is, and why it is being made, with enough context for anyone to understand. -->

<details>
  <summary>PR Checklist</summary>
  
### PR Structure

* [ ] This PR has reasonably narrow scope (if not, break it down into smaller PRs).
* [ ] This PR avoids mixing refactoring changes with feature changes (split into two PRs
  otherwise).
* [ ] This PR's title starts with name of package that is most changed in the PR, ex.
  `services/friendbot`, or `all` or `doc` if the changes are broad or impact many
  packages.

### Thoroughness

* [ ] This PR adds tests for the most critical parts of the new functionality or fixes.
* [ ] I've updated any docs ([developer docs](https://developers.stellar.org/api/), `.md`
  files, etc... affected by this change). Take a look in the `docs` folder for a given service,
  like [this one](https://github.com/stellar/go/tree/master/services/horizon/internal/docs).

### Release planning

* [ ] I've reviewed the changes in this PR and if I consider them worthwhile for being mentioned on release notes then I have updated the relevant `CHANGELOG.md` within the  component folder structure. For example, if I changed horizon, then I updated ([services/horizon/CHANGELOG.md](services/horizon/CHANGELOG.md). I add a new line item describing the change and reference to this PR. If I don't update a CHANGELOG, I acknowledge this PR's change may not be mentioned in future release notes.  
* [ ] I've decided if this PR requires a new major/minor version according to
  [semver](https://semver.org/), or if it's mainly a patch change. The PR is targeted at the next
  release branch if it's not a patch change.
</details>

### What

Refactors the app.Run() to use `errgroup.WithContext` and `signal.NotifyContext` for simpler unified shutdown behavior.

The advantage of using `errgroup.WithContext` is that it automatically cancels the context when any goroutine returns an error. Similarly, `signal.NotifyContext` automatically cancels the context when the process receives an OS signal.


Also, as discussed [here](https://github.com/stellar/go/pull/5820#discussion_r2543619121) we don’t need to cancel the context when LoadTest completes, so we return nil instead of an error.

## Hybrid Storage Implementation - Code Review Fixes

Addressed all actionable feedback from the code review:

### Changes Made
- [x] Fix syntax error in useLocalStorage.ts (missing closing parenthesis)
- [x] Fix useLocalStorage to handle localStorage.clear() events
- [x] Fix useRepositoryData to use useMemo instead of calling function on every render
- [x] Fix setValue callback dependencies to avoid stale closures
- [x] Remove unused variables in CheckoutPage and ProductDetailPage
- [x] Verify build and linter pass
- [x] Improve storage event handler clarity with explicit case handling

### Technical Improvements

**useLocalStorage.ts**
- Fixed missing closing parenthesis that was causing syntax error
- Updated storage event handler to handle `localStorage.clear()` (when `e.key === null`)
- Restructured event handler with explicit case handling for better code clarity:
  - Case 1: `localStorage.clear()` called (`e.key === null`)
  - Case 2: Key was updated (`e.key === key && e.newValue !== null`)
  - Case 3: Key was removed (`e.key === key && e.newValue === null`)

**useRepositoryData.ts**
- Changed `mergedData` from `useCallback` to `useMemo` to avoid recalculation on every render
- Fixed `setValue` callback to compute merged data inline using functional state update
- Removed dependency on `mergedData` callback, using `repoData` and `isLoading` directly
- This prevents setValue from being recreated unnecessarily and fixes stale closure issues

**Unused Variables**
- CheckoutPage.tsx: Changed `orders` to `_` (not used, only setter is needed)
- ProductDetailPage.tsx: Changed `cart` to `_` (not used, only setter is needed)

### Testing
✅ Build succeeds with no errors
✅ Linter passes (19 warnings, all pre-existing)
✅ All hook dependencies are now stable
✅ No performance regressions from unnecessary re-renders

### Notes on Other Review Comments

**Not Addressed (Intentional Design Choices):**
- Storing full dataset in localStorage - This is intentional for the current admin workflow
- Hardcoded data URLs - Acceptable for this deployment setup, can be refactored later if needed
- No error state for failed JSON loads - Falls back to empty array, which is acceptable UX for now

These represent architectural decisions that work for the current use case and can be revisited in future iterations if needed.

        - Docstring explains it decodes and validates a JWT and lets decode errors propagate.
    - Removed the redundant try/except that re-raised the same exceptions.
    - Now simply:
        - return jwt.decode(access_token, JWT_SECRET, algorithms=["HS256"])
- /middleware/auth_middleware.py
    - Removed the broad except Exception as ex.
    - Imported jwt and now only catches JWT-related errors:
        - except (jwt.ExpiredSignatureError, jwt.InvalidTokenError) as ex:
        - These are translated to HTTPException(status_code=401, detail=str(ex)) with from ex to preserve tracebacks.
    - Other unexpected errors will now propagate rather than being turned into 401s.

author: sandytao520
body:
## TLDR

This PR fixes an issue where clicking on wide characters (e.g., CJK characters) in the input prompt would position the cursor incorrectly. Previously, the logic assumed a 1:1 mapping between visual columns and character indices, which is incorrect for characters taking up multiple columns.

## Dive Deeper

The `moveToVisualPosition` function in `text-buffer.ts` was updated to correctly calculate the logical cursor position from a visual click coordinate.
*   It now iterates through the characters of the line, summing up their visual widths (using `string-width`).
*   It checks if the clicked column falls within a character's visual range.
*   If the click is on the second half of a wide character (width >= 2), it snaps the cursor to the *after* position of that character.
*   `preferredCol` is updated to track the logical character offset rather than the raw visual column, improving vertical navigation consistency across lines with mixed character widths.

## Reviewer Test Plan

1.  Open the CLI.
2.  Type some wide characters, e.g., "你好世界" (Hello World in Chinese).
3.  Click on the left half of '好'. The cursor should appear between '你' and '好'.
4.  Click on the right half of '好'. The cursor should appear between '好' and '世'.
5.  Verify that clicking on regular ASCII text still works as expected.

author: defymecobra
body: # Add HeatmapChart Widget for Cohort Analysis ## Overview This PR introduces a new `HeatmapChart` widget that enables cohort analysis visualization using ECharts heatmap. The widget displays retention, churn, LTV, and other cohort-based metrics in a triangular heatmap format with automatic "Total" row calculation. ## Changes ### API Definition Added `HeatmapChart` C# record and TypeScript interfaces to define the widget contract. The API includes properties for `Data`, `Title`, `MetricType` (currency/percentage/number), `ShowTotal`, and optional `Toolbox` configuration. ### Widget Implementation Implemented `HeatmapChartWidget` React component using ECharts heatmap with full theme integration. The widget features an Emerald gradient color scheme that adapts to light/dark mode, automatic data processing with period/cohort extraction, and smart label formatting based on metric type. ### Auto-calculated Total Row Added optional "Total" row functionality that automatically aggregates values across all cohorts for each period. This feature is controlled via the `ShowTotal` property and calculates sums on the frontend to reduce backend complexity. ### Demo Application Created `HeatmapChartApp` sample application showcasing four real-world use cases: Retention Rate, LTV per User, Churn Rate, and MRR per Cohort. Each example demonstrates different metric types and formatting options.

author: hoxyq
body:
Summary:
# Changelog: [Internal]

Introduces a TracingDelegate that will receive tracing-related events on the Host side.

We can't give synchronous access to tracing state to Host directly, since there is no guarantee that this call will happen on the inspector thread.

Example:
- `HostTarget::tracingState()` call may happen on UI thread, or whatever thread the Host is using, which reads `traceRecoding_` value.
- At the same time, the `stopTracing()` call that will invalidate `traceRecording_` could happen on inspector thread.

This is a pre-requisite for a better threading model, since we are going to be doing much frequent write operations from the Host side to record frame timings or screenshots.

Differential Revision: D86205686
